questions.q: 'The box of apples ___ (is/are) on the shelf.'
questions.a: 'is' — head is 'box'. A wrong answer 'are' is proximity agreement — matching the verb to 'apples', the decoy standing closest.
'was' — 'along with' is a comma-insert; it does not pluralize. A wrong answer 'were' shows the and-equivalence error.

questions.q: 'There ___ (is/are) a dog and two cats in the yard.'
questions.a: 'are' — compound subject after 'there' takes plural (boards expect 'are'). A wrong answer 'is' applies proximity where the rule requires summing.

questions.q: ______ phrases between subject and verb are grammatically invisible.
Fill in the blank: The verb agrees with the head of the subject, not with ______ noun stands nearest. 'The bunch of keys IS on the table' — 'bunch' is the head, 'keys' is a decoy inside an of-phrase.

Fill in the blank: The insert rule: 'as well as', 'along with', 'together with' do NOT make the subject plural — they are passengers in commas. 'There' ______ invert: the real subject follows the verb — 'There ARE three eggs left.'
What must you be able to do to master this topic?
questions.a: The student locates the head noun through of-phrases and parenthetical inserts, chooses the matching verb form, and handles 'there is/are' inversion.

questions.q: Fill in the blank: Strip ______: 'The colour of the walls ___ (is/are) fading.' Delete 'of the walls' → 'the colour IS fading'.
